root_cause: The critical path traverses from primary activation inputs directly through unpipelined PE MAC arithmetic (an 8x8 signed multiplier and a 32-bit adder) in a single cycle, resulting in timing failure at 150 MHz.
architecture_change: Partitioned the PE microarchitecture into two pipeline stages (Stage A: multiplication/alignment, Stage B: INT32 accumulation). Added synchronous boundary input registers at the array level to isolate external input delays from internal systolic arithmetic. Increased activation and partial-sum hop latencies to 2 cycles each, uniformly preserving structural wavefront alignment.
timing_reasoning: Separating the signed INT8 multiplication and INT32 accumulation into discrete pipeline stages aggressively reduces the internal combinational depth of the processing element.
Synchronous array-boundary input registers eliminate the reported timing startpoint issue, decoupling input port delay from internal PE arithmetic.
Pipelining the primary inputs (act_in and psum_in) into an alignment register alongside the product ensures both dimensions of the systolic wavefront remain logically and mathematically aligned.
